EDITORIAL METHOD / v0.4.4

Evidence before
certainty.

Evidence → decision → counter-check → translation → review → versioned publication.

  1. Register the source, rights, date and textual scope.
  2. Distinguish manuscript transcription from a modern edited display.
  3. Keep normalized text, restored text, retroversion and conjecture distinct.
  4. Compare individual readings and ancient editions; do not privilege a manuscript solely because it is older.
  5. Record the strongest counterargument and select the current best translation; keep unresolved historical details separately identified.
  6. Translate from the stated Hebrew basis, distinguishing a manuscript display from an editorial reconstruction; label every alternative reading.
  7. Request independent review and record corrections. Specialist review remains a separate requirement.

This collection

Complete MT-WLC verses are provided as comparison displays; selected translations state their own textual basis. No complete independent collation of these passages has been performed. Deuteronomy 32:8 now selects the divine-sons reading provisionally. Its full translation is an editorial reconstruction using the MT remainder and a reported 4Q37 phrase, rather than a complete 4Q37 verse or a new photograph reading.

Layers and rights

WLC Hebrew text is public domain. OSHB morphology and lemmas are credited under CC BY 4.0. Display removes morpheme separators and adapts punctuation spacing while preserving vowel/accent codepoints. The three translations and notes are fresh AI-assisted editorial drafts. Selected glosses are illustrative, not a complete word-aligned interlinear.

Corrections

Report the passage ID, version, source and proposed correction through the repository. New evidence can reopen a decision; the previous release remains identifiable.
